source: Kaur, Adar, Gilbert, Lampe (2022) Sensible AI: Re-imagining Interpretability and Explainability using Sensemaking Theory
finding: Maps all seven Weick properties onto ML explanation design. Argues an instant explanation skips retrospective sensemaking, so users build a plausible story that agrees with the model instead of checking it.
numbers: Conceptual, 20 pages, FAccT 2022. No experiment. Worked examples: radiologist with saliency maps, PredPol patrol allocation, HR candidate ranking.
quote: Given plausible explanations for a prediction, people are not inclined to search for the accurate one
limits: Conceptual only; no measured effects. Weick's eight reasons accuracy is secondary are cited, not tested on a model.
agent_relevance: Shows how to read plausibility-over-accuracy as a risk in an LLM explanation: a fluent rationale is read as a verified one. Supports forcing a check step before showing a rationale.

source: Turpin, Michael, Perez, Bowman (2023) Language Models Don't Always Say What They Think: Unfaithful CoT
finding: Biasing the prompt (answer always A, or a stereotype cue) changes model answers, and the chain of thought rationalises the biased answer without naming the bias. This is plausibility without accuracy in a machine.
numbers: GPT-3.5 and Claude 1.0 on 13 BIG-Bench Hard tasks: accuracy drops up to 36% under bias. Unbiased CoT vs no-CoT: 57.1 to 59.6 (GPT-3.5), 59.2 to 65.3 (Claude 1.0). Of 104 annotated unfaithful cases, explanations changed to support the wrong answer in up to 73%. On BBQ, 86% of stereotype-aligned answers had an explanation supporting them.
quote: CoT explanations can be plausible yet misleading
limits: Old models (2023). Debiasing instruction nearly removed BBQ bias for Claude 1.0 (62.5 to 50.6) but not for GPT-3.5 zero-shot.
agent_relevance: A rationale from the agent is a story, not evidence of its process. Do not use the agent's own explanation as proof a step was sound.

source: Arcuschin et al. (2026, ICML) Chain-of-Thought Reasoning in the Wild Is Not Always Faithful
finding: On plain, non-adversarial prompts, models write coherent arguments to answer Yes to both 'X bigger than Y' and 'Y bigger than X'. Called Implicit Post-Hoc Rationalization.
numbers: 4,834 question pairs, 15 frontier models plus one pretrained. Rates: GPT-4o-mini 13.49%, Haiku 3.5 7.42%, DeepSeek R1 0.37%, Sonnet 3.7 with thinking 0.04%. Llama 3.1 70B pretrained 3.25% vs instruct 2.09%. GPT-4o-mini stable across temperature (13.1, 13.7, 12.7%).
limits: Pair-consistency test; detects only contradiction, not all rationalisation. Thinking models much lower but not zero.
agent_relevance: Retrospective story-building is a default model behaviour. Pairing a claim with its mirror claim is a cheap consistency probe the loop could use.

source: Lanham et al. (2023) Measuring Faithfulness in Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
finding: Intervening on the CoT (truncating, adding mistakes, paraphrasing) shows models differ widely in how much they rely on the stated reasoning. Larger models give less faithful reasoning on most tasks.
numbers: Faithfulness worsens from 13B to 175B on 7 of 8 tasks (inverse scaling). CoT gain is not from extra compute or phrasing alone.
limits: Anthropic models of 2023 only; 8 multiple-choice tasks.
agent_relevance: The more capable the model, the more its stated reasoning may be after-the-fact. Treat CoT as retrospective narrative; test it by intervention.

source: Shinn et al. (2023) Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
finding: A retrospective loop: after a failed trial the agent writes a verbal reflection stored in memory and retries. Closest working agent analogue of Weick's retrospect plus enactment (act, look back, re-act).
numbers: AlfWorld 134 tasks: +22% absolute in 12 iterative steps over ReAct baseline. HotPotQA +20%. HumanEval Python pass@1 91.0 vs GPT-4 80.1. Binary environment success signal used between trials.
limits: Gains rely on an external success signal (tests, environment). Authors admit flaky self-written tests can give false positives.
agent_relevance: Retrospect works when grounded by an external check. Pure self-retrospect without a signal is weak (see c06).

source: Huang et al. (2024, ICLR) Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet
finding: Without external feedback, asking the model to review its own answer does not help and often hurts. The model cannot judge whether its own story is correct.
numbers: GPT-3.5 on GSM8K: 75.9 initial, 75.1 after round 1, 74.7 after round 2. Among changed answers, more went correct-to-incorrect than the reverse. CommonSenseQA: more answers altered, many correct-to-incorrect.
limits: Intrinsic self-correction only, with GPT-3.5, GPT-4, Llama-2. Oracle-label stopping inflates gains in earlier papers.
agent_relevance: Retrospect without a cue from outside the model adds plausibility, not accuracy. Pair every retrospective step with an external cue.

source: Mooney, Kim, Lee, Kang (2026) Structure Liberates: How Constrained Sensemaking Produces More Novel Research Output (SciSense)
finding: Uses the Pirolli-Card eight-stage sensemaking loop to train research-ideation models. Hindsight data (path reconstructed backward from a known paper, a retrospective account) beats Foresight data (open-ended forward ideas) on quality and diversity.
numbers: 120K trajectories; models 3B to 70B, eight families. Hindsight gains 2.0% aggregate plan quality over Foresight and is most diverse under every automatic metric in all eight families. Downstream coding agent (gpt-5.3-codex) scored higher on executability, grounding, utility with Hindsight plans; every distilled variant beat No-Plan and Direct-Prompt baselines.
limits: Pirolli-Card, not Weick. Judge is an LLM. Hindsight plans are LLM reconstructions, not real researcher histories.
agent_relevance: Evidence that retrospectively-built structure helps downstream action, in line with Weick's retrospect. Outcome-anchored plans beat open-ended ones.

source: Dammu, Palkhiwala, Roosta, Shah (2026) iAgentBench: Benchmarking Sensemaking Capabilities of Information-Seeking Agents
finding: Benchmark of cross-source sensemaking questions built from a story graph of themes and connectors. Retrieval helps, but integration across themes stays hard; self-reflection sometimes hurts.
numbers: 500 sampled questions per benchmark (SimpleQA, HotpotQA, iAgentBench); Claude Sonnet 4.5, Llama 4 Maverick, Mistral Large 3, Gemma 3 27B; Base, RAG, Reflexion. Example SimpleQA Claude Sonnet 4.5: Base 0.240, RAG 0.740. Reflexion gain over RAG ranged from negative (about -0.07) to about +0.17 depending on model and set.
quote: Refl is mixed: Reflexion can improve over RAG ... but it can also regress
limits: Table text garbled in my extraction; model-to-cell mapping is approximate. Uses the word sensemaking in the Edge et al. query-focused sense, not Weick's.
agent_relevance: Reflexion-style iteration can cause drift or over-correction. Gate any retrospective loop by whether it adds new evidence.

source: Jain (2026) Collaborative Causal Sensemaking: Closing the Complementarity Gap in Human-AI Decision Support
finding: Position paper: LLM agents are trained as answer engines, not partners in sensemaking. Cites Weick 1995. Notes sycophancy collapses to the user's prior, which is fatal for sensemaking that needs repair of mental models.
numbers: No new experiment. Survey claim: human-AI teams in subjective, costly-to-verify domains often underperform the best single agent.
limits: Research agenda; no data of its own.
agent_relevance: Names sycophancy as the main machine-side break of the 'social' and 'identity' properties. Background only.

source: Sindelar and Bojar (2025) Overview of the Sensemaking Task at ELOQUENT 2025
finding: Teacher, Student, Evaluator shared task. LLM judges accept nonsense answers: they rate garbled or mismatched question-answer pairs as acceptable, a plausible-over-accurate pattern.
numbers: 7 material kinds, 4 languages, 4 teams. Baseline GPT-4.1-nano evaluator rating fell only from 65 to 49 on nonsensical adversarial questions. Evaluator agreement about 60% on adversarial items vs about 70% on normal. ROUGE-L class agreement about 0.33 (chance for 3 classes).
limits: Sensemaking here = text comprehension, not Weick. Small field (2 teacher, 2 student, 2 evaluator submissions).
agent_relevance: An LLM checking another LLM's story is not a real cue. Disagreement between judges may flag bad items.

source: Suh et al. (2023) Sensecape: Multilevel Exploration and Sensemaking with LLMs
finding: Human-LLM tool that externalises a hierarchy of concepts. Within-subjects study against ChatGPT plus canvas baseline.
numbers: N=12. Concepts explored: 68.3 (SD 49.1) vs 22.8 (SD 7.7), t(11)=3.1, p=0.01. Hierarchy levels: 4.3 vs 2.6, p=0.02. Revisits: 12.8 vs 0.7. Prompts, nodes, links did not differ.
limits: Small N, two topics, built on Pirolli-Card. Not a test of Weick's properties.
agent_relevance: Externalised, revisitable structure raises ongoing sensemaking. Suggests a persistent map across turns.

source: Liu, Wu, Chen, Li, et al. (2023) Selenite: Scaffolding Online Sensemaking with Comprehensive Overviews Elicited from LLMs
finding: LLM-elicited overview of options and criteria cues the reader. Readers finished faster and held more, better criteria.
numbers: Study 2 N=12 within-subjects: time 840.3 s vs 1319.3 s (36.3% faster, F(1,20)=102.5). Valid criteria +90.4% (12.93 mean). Precision 98.8% vs 78.4%; recall 73.0% vs 30.4% (p<0.05). Option extraction 100% accurate in Study 1.
limits: Small N, planned topics, designed by authors of the tool.
agent_relevance: Cue extraction by an LLM measurably helps humans. Cues are one of Weick's seven properties.

source: Wolter, Haag, Dhanoa, Elmqvist (2026) Context-Mediated Domain Adaptation in Multi-Agent Sensemaking Systems (Seedentia)
finding: Multi-agent LLM tool learns from experts' edits to its output and re-injects patterns in later prompts.
numbers: N=5 experts; 46 domain-knowledge entries extracted from edits. Authors say the sample is too small to claim systematic quality gains.
limits: Exploratory; no effect size.
agent_relevance: Edit-derived memory is an 'ongoing plus social' loop. No evidence yet it improves answers.

source: Ubellacker (2025) Making Sense of AI Limitations: Individual Perceptions and Organizational Readiness
finding: Interviews analysed with the Gioia method, framed on Weick. Hands-on experience with AI limits gave more realistic expectations and more trust, especially with peer networks and champions.
numbers: 7 expert interviews; saturation judged at seven (interviews 4-7 added 11-25 new codes each).
limits: Tiny purposive sample; master's thesis origin; no quantitative test.
agent_relevance: Humans adjust trust through enacted use of the tool. Background for deployment, not for the loop.

source: Sudeeptha, Mueller, Leyer, Richter, Nolte (2024) Use Cases for Prospective Sensemaking of Human-AI-Collaboration
finding: Uses use-case mapping as a prospective sensemaking tool in a car maker.
numbers: 14 executive interviews at one automotive company.
limits: One firm; feedback was qualitative.
agent_relevance: Weick's retrospect has a forward twin. Little to take for a single agent.

source: Gogoll (2026) The Ethical Knowledge Gap: Dispersed Knowledge, Sensemaking Failures, and Epistemic Dependence
finding: Uses Weick 1995 and Weick, Sutcliffe, Obstfeld 2005 to argue that software teams lack categories to notice ethical cues. Organisations shape what counts as a plausible description.
numbers: Conceptual; no data.
limits: Diagnostic essay only.
agent_relevance: A model with no category for a cue will not see it. Supports checking which cues the prompt makes salient.

source: Weick, Sutcliffe, Obstfeld (2005) Organizing and the Process of Sensemaking
finding: Core restatement: sensemaking as noticing, bracketing, labelling, then action that creates the sense. Cited by c15 and c16, which I opened.
numbers: Cited only. No numbers read this session.
limits: Not opened.
agent_relevance: Background.

source: Pirolli and Card (2005) The Sensemaking Process and Leverage Points for Analyst Technology
finding: Foraging loop and sensemaking loop model used by Sensecape and SciSense (c07, c11).
numbers: Cited only. Eight stages as listed in SciSense (c07).
limits: Not opened; read only through the papers that use it.
agent_relevance: Computational template for a loop that Weick leaves non-procedural.

source: Edge et al. (2024) From Local to Global: GraphRAG
finding: Defines global sensemaking queries over a whole corpus that standard RAG fails on. iAgentBench (c08) builds on it.
numbers: Not opened; claim taken from c08.
limits: Not opened.
agent_relevance: Different meaning of sensemaking from Weick.

source: Technology-mediated sensemaking: the role of GenAI (LIUC conference paper)
finding: Applies the Weick et al. 2005 enactment model to GenAI chatbot use in equivocal organisational settings.
numbers: Search snippet only; no numbers.
limits: Not opened.
agent_relevance: The Weick lens is now used on chatbot use, not tested on model behaviour.

source: Artificial intelligence and work transformations: integrating sensemaking and workplace learning (Information Technology and People)
finding: 23 focus groups at four Swedish manufacturing firms: how perceived AI features trigger initial sensemaking.
numbers: 23 focus groups, 4 firms (search snippet).
limits: Not opened.
agent_relevance: Background on human-side adoption.

source: Search finding 2026-11-17: no study treats an LLM as a Weick sensemaker
finding: Searches found no paper that tests the seven properties, Mann Gulch or Bhopal analogues, or enactment against LLM behaviour. Closest are c01 (conceptual) and c02-c06 (indirect).
numbers: About 20 arXiv queries and 1 web search. arXiv partly rate-limited; OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar quota exhausted.
limits: Absence of evidence in limited search; not a systematic review.
agent_relevance: The Weick link to our agent rests on indirect tests: unfaithful rationale, self-correction failure, Reflexion with external signal.

source: Madaan et al. (2023) Self-Refine
finding: Iterative self-feedback improves outputs on many tasks; Huang et al. (c06) argue gains vanish without oracle information.
numbers: Not opened; relation to c06 stated in c06.
limits: Not opened.
agent_relevance: Same retrospect-without-cue caveat.

source: Park et al. (2023) Generative Agents
finding: Agents store memories and periodically write reflections, then plan from them. A retrospective-summary loop in a simulated social world.
numbers: Not opened; from prior knowledge.
limits: Not verified this session.
agent_relevance: Model for ongoing, social retrospect in an agent loop.

source: Weick (1993) The Collapse of Sensemaking in Organizations: The Mann Gulch Disaster
finding: Founding case: smokejumpers died when roles and the meaning of the fire collapsed; the foreman's escape fire went unrecognised.
numbers: Case study; no numbers read (13 deaths, from memory).
limits: Not opened. A single narrative, not a test.
agent_relevance: Agent analogue: frame collapse when a cue breaks the plan; dropping the plan is the survival move.

source: Reading of c02, c03, c04: plausibility over accuracy in models
finding: Across Turpin, Lanham and Arcuschin the model's story is fluent whether or not it is right. Matches Weick's claim that a good story needs coherence, not accuracy.
numbers: See c02, c03, c04.
limits: My reading, not a published test.
agent_relevance: Design principle: require an external cue before accepting a story.

source: Synthesis of c05 and c06: Reflexion vs intrinsic self-correction
finding: Both study retrospect. Reflexion gains rely on an environment signal; Huang shows no gain without one. Together: retrospect plus enactment (act in the world, get a cue) works; retrospect alone does not.
numbers: c05: +22% AlfWorld; c06: 75.9 to 74.7 on GSM8K.
limits: My synthesis; models and tasks differ.
agent_relevance: Strongest design lesson from this angle.
